description:
Mission: We are tackling the harmonization of MODIS and VIIR challenges to build automated pipeline and visualization dashboard for active fire monitoring.

About Us: We are passionate about space systems and remote sensing, aiming to deliver a functional, well-documented prototype.
summary: PyroSync helps people understand why different satellites can tell different stories about fire activity. Using NASA FIRMS observations from MODIS and VIIRS, we built a working dashboard for Sri Lanka and Argentina that combines an activity calendar, a map, source evidence, and downloadable briefs. A shared counting rule records each active grid cell once per day while preserving the observations behind it. Users can inspect sensor differences and see how results change when a source or analytical choice changes. Historical sensor mappings improve agreement with a VIIRS observation reference in both countries. We also evaluate seven-day forecasts against simple baselines using earlier data for model selection and later years for testing. Historical results are promising in Argentina, while Sri Lanka’s gains remain inconclusive. PyroSync is a research prototype, not a live emergency-warning service. Our goal is to help analysts compare, question, and explain satellite fire records before those records inform decisions.
details:
The problem

Different satellites can give very different pictures of fire activity. In our Sri Lanka data for 2025, MODIS recorded 684 observations, while VIIRS on Suomi-NPP recorded 5,519. This does not mean eight times as many separate fires occurred. Instrument resolution, observation times, and repeated views affect the numbers.

Our solution

PyroSync helps users compare these observations and inspect the evidence behind them. Our working dashboard covers Sri Lanka and Argentina. Users select a country and month, explore an activity calendar, read a plain-language period brief, inspect mapped observations, and download their results.

We divide the land into small grid cells. A cell with at least one qualifying vegetation detection on a UTC day counts once for that day: one “active cell-day.” We preserve contributing satellite sources, timestamps, and original CSV row references. These units describe recorded activity, rather than separate fire incidents or burned area.

What makes the approach useful

PyroSync connects the calendar, geographic evidence, source comparisons, and downloadable briefs. Users can remove a satellite source or change analytical settings to see how much a result depends on those choices. Static thermal sources are shown separately from vegetation activity.

Measured evidence

Our historical work uses 30 NASA archive files containing almost three million source records from 2020–2024.

Using mappings selected with earlier data, error against the VIIRS observation reference was reduced relative to unmapped MODIS by:

• Sri Lanka: 29.5% in 2023 and 18.5% in 2024.
• Argentina: 61.4% in 2023 and 50.3% in 2024.

VIIRS is a reference observation record, not verified ground truth. Exploratory simulated sensor-switch checks also showed smaller reference-relative discontinuities after mapping.

For seven-day forecasts, Argentina’s selected model reduced average error against the last-week baseline by 19.2% in 2023 and 31.9% in 2024. Sri Lanka’s forecast improvements remained inconclusive. Both original 2025 country selections failed our promotion checks, and those outcomes remain visible.

Development and verification

Within the 48-hour hackathon, we built and checked the complete workflow. The project passes 44 automated tests and 14 browser checks covering both countries, count consistency, downloads, keyboard interactions, and mobile layout.

The analysis uses Python, NumPy, and H3. The interface uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SVG. A separate MiroFish communication experiment uses Gemini through Vertex AI and Zep; its generated discussion remains separate from observation facts and numerical forecasts.

Impact and next steps

Our intended users include fire analysts, researchers, environmental teams, and report writers. We want to help them investigate surprising numbers and share conclusions with supporting evidence. Next steps include analyst feedback, better observation-coverage information, and validation across real sensor transitions. Operational warning accuracy and user benefits have not yet been established.

SI/AI disclosure

OpenAI Codex/ChatGPT assisted architecture, research, coding, documentation, interface design, and submission preparation. Google Gemini through Vertex AI supported the synthetic communication experiment and generated the adult synthetic narration using Gemini 2.5 Pro TTS with the Charon voice. The demo includes visible SI disclosure and embedded narration metadata. NASA observations are source data, not SI-generated data. No NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers were generated or modified.
